article.articleHeadline: WHO calls for a united response to Ebola outbreak in Africa
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-23, the WHO Africa region director calls for a united response to the Ebola outbreak. Nigeria reports its first Ebola case, identified as imported. Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo are handling cases linked to the Bundibugyo strain. Janabi emphasizes coordinated action to prevent further spread, urging governments, partners, communities and citizens to act early, find cases quickly, establish contact tracing, support health workers and caring communities, and share information. With trust, responses are stronger; borders should be lines of cooperation, not vulnerability. The briefing underscores the need for rapid case detection, tracing, and cross-border coordination to curb transmission amid this ongoing outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、アフリカでのエボラ出血熱流行に対する統一的対応を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC、ウガンダ、ケニアで継続し、ナイジェリアに輸入例が発生するなど複数国にまたがる拡大が確認されており、WHOが国際的な統一対応を呼びかけている。IHR基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア（輸入例）、ウガンダ、ケニアでも症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCのブンディブギョ株に関連した複数国間の感染拡大が主題。

article.articleHeadline: ولاية غرب الاستوائية تقف ميدانياً على جاهزية وحدة مكافحة إيبولا بيامبيو - Radio Tamazuj
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Western Equatoria State on the ground assesses the readiness of the Ebola Control Unit in Yambio
article.articleSummary: On 23 October 2026, Western Equatoria State in South Sudan conducted a readiness assessment of the Ebola Control Unit in Yambio. The Infectious Diseases Unit (IDU)/Ebola Treatment Unit (ETU) was inspected by a delegation led by Acting Governor Badagbo Daniel Rumbasa to evaluate its capacity to screen, isolate suspected Ebola cases, prevent transmission, and safeguard health workers. A simulated drill tested emergency response and surveillance procedures. The visit included State Health Minister Nema Pokolo, security officials, partners, and staff from the International Medical Corps, WHO, UNICEF, and the National Public Health Institute in Juba. The facility has 28 beds across four wards, with a red isolation zone and green zones for staff, plus a pharmacy, ambulance bay, staff housing, and psychosocial space. South Sudan has had no Ebola cases to date; cross-border risk from the Democratic Republic of Congo was highlighted.

triage.headline_ja: 西エクアトリア州、ヤンビオにあるエボラ対策ユニットの即応態勢を現地視察
triage.triage_reason: 南スーダンでのエボラ症例は報告されておらず、本記事は対策準備の視察に関する内容だが、コンゴ民主共和国からの越境リスクが指摘されており、地域の警戒レベルとして経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は南スーダン（対象国リスト外）での準備態勢視察であり、実際のエボラ症例発生はないため南スーダンは対象外。DRCは越境リスクの文脈で言及されているのみで、DRC国内での発生報告ではないため参考情報として記載するが、厳密には主題国ではない点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Prevenção: casos de sarampo em outros países reforçam alerta para vacinação em MS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Prevention: Measles cases in other countries reinforce the call for vaccination in MS.
article.articleSummary: Measles in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil shows no confirmed cases in 2026 as of September 1, but 24 suspected cases (23 ruled out, 1 under investigation). First-dose coverage is 97.10% and second-dose 81.79%, highlighting the need to complete the second dose. A September 2026 multisector vaccination campaign delivered 84,439 doses, including about 4,262 measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) doses. An upcoming Aluno Imunizado school-based vaccination drive in November will vaccinate students and issue an Up-to-Date Vaccination Declaration (DVA). Indigenous programs include D0 vaccination for 6–11 month-olds in DSEIs and strengthened surveillance across 34 DSEIs. History: last MS measles confirmations in 2020 (10 in Campo Grande); 2019 had 4 cases. International context: the US reports nearly 4,000 cases in 2026; the Americas account for 99.5% of regional cases, with Brazil reporting 61 imported or import-related cases. Vaccination is free via SUS, with D1 at 12 months and D2 at 15 months.

triage.headline_ja: 予防：他国での麻疹症例を受け、MS州でワクチン接種の呼びかけを強化
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・マトグロッソドスル州では2026年の確定症例はゼロで、予防接種率も高く、ワクチンキャンペーンが順調に進められている予防的な内容の記事であり、シグナルとしての緊急性はない。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル国内（マトグロッソドスル州）のワクチン接種啓発と予防活動が主題で、確定症例は無く、米国など国際情勢は参考情報として言及されているのみ。米国・スペイン（カナリア諸島）は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: डेंगू नहीं; सामान्य बुखार... फिर भी घट रहीं प्लेटलेट्स, शामली में सामने आ रहे ऐसे मामले
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Not dengue; a common fever... Yet platelet counts are falling, such cases are emerging in Shamli.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 October 2026, Shamli district, Uttar Pradesh, India, is seeing fever patients with rapidly falling platelet counts (thrombocytopenia). Dengue is not the sole cause; many cases show low platelets without dengue confirmation. Over-the-counter analgesic use without medical advice is identified as a potential factor, along with other viral infections and health conditions. Dr. Sachin Malik, a physician at the district hospital, warns that self-medication for fever, body aches, and headaches can increase bleeding risk and impair platelet function due to unknown dosages and side effects. In rural areas, similar patterns are observed. The outpatient department reports 50-60 patients daily with low platelets. Public health messaging emphasizes avoiding arbitrary painkiller use and seeking medical evaluation for fever or thrombocytopenia.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱ではない；普通の発熱…それでも血小板数が減少、シャームリーでこうした症例が発生
triage.triage_reason: 発熱と血小板減少の症例が増加しているが、デング熱など特定の病原体確認はなく、自己服薬が主な要因として指摘されており、明確な感染症アウトブレイクとは言い難いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱やSFTSウイルスへの直接的な言及がなく、むしろ血小板減少の原因としての自己服薬（鎮痛剤乱用）に焦点を当てている。疾患名タグ（SFTS、Dengue）は記事内容と一致しない可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: MDCAN urges hospitals to activate isolation centres, boost surveillance
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease case confirmed in Nigeria: one imported case in Abuja (Federal Capital Territory), a woman with recent travel to Uganda. Symptoms began Oct 7; she sought care Oct 11 and laboratory confirmation occurred on Oct 20. Nigeria becomes the fifth country to detect Bundibugyo virus since the Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak began on May 15, 2026. The patient is in isolation and receiving care; the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has activated its incident management system to coordinate the response. The Medical and Dental Consultants' Association of Nigeria (MDCAN) urged activation of infectious disease isolation centres, strengthened surveillance, contact tracing, and cross-border collaboration at airports, seaports, and land borders; improved laboratory capacity and hospital preparedness; PPE, diagnostic materials, running water, infrared thermometers, and trained staff; reactivation of IPC committees and isolation areas; and public messaging to report cases promptly and avoid bushmeat. Symptoms to watch include fever, severe headache, vomiting, diarrhoea, bleeding, or contact with a suspected case.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：MDCAN(ナイジェリア医科・歯科コンサルタント協会)、病院に隔離施設の稼働とサーベイランス強化を要請
triage.triage_reason: DRCで続くエボラ(ブンディブギョウイルス)流行に関連し、ナイジェリアで輸入症例が確認され国際的拡大が継続している。IHR基準複数該当し、社会的・行政的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事はナイジェリアでの輸入症例（渡航歴のある女性）を主に報じているが、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。2026年5月15日に開始したDRCでのブンディブギョウイルス流行が背景として明記されており、DRCを発生国として含めた。ウガンダも言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Uncertainty Over Source Of Nigeria's First Case As WHO Sounds Alarm Over 'Complex' Africa Spread, FG Quarantines High-Risk Contacts
article.articleSummary: On 23 October 2026, Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola Virus Disease case, a Bundibugyo strain, making Nigeria the fourth African country affected after the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and Kenya. The index patient is a Ugandan-born woman in Abuja, married to a Swiss diplomat; she arrived asymptomatic and developed illness days later. Laboratory results show significant improvement, with officials saying a full recovery is possible, and there is currently no evidence of community transmission. The source remains unresolved; authorities characterize the case as imported while travel histories are being reconstructed. Africa CDC notes Nigeria’s index patient and Kenya’s first Ebola patient both departed Entebbe on 3 October, raising questions about potential encounters. Nigeria quarantined high-risk contacts, traced hospital and private-facility exposures, activated the incident management system, and urged states to bolster bed capacity and strict infection prevention and control.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：ナイジェリア初症例の感染源不明、WHOはアフリカでの『複雑な』拡大に警鐘、政府は高リスク接触者を隔離
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大）に該当し、WHOが『複雑なアフリカ拡大』として警鐘を鳴らしており社会的関心も高いため、フルリスク評価に進むべき事案と判断する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアでの初症例確認だが、ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは現在進行中の複数国にまたがるエボラアウトブレイクの発生国の一つとして言及されているため含めた。ウガンダ出国者がケニアとナイジェリアの症例に関連する可能性がAfrica CDCにより指摘されており、感染経路の解明が続報として重要。

article.articleHeadline: Cúm A gia tăng, cảnh giác với tình trạng tự ý dùng Tamiflu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A on the rise; beware of self-medication with Tamiflu.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A is rising in Hanoi, with the Hanoi CDC reporting 200–300 influenza A cases weekly seeking medical care. Most infections are mild, but influenza A can worsen, especially in children, the elderly, and those with chronic diseases. Tamiflu (oseltamivir) is drawing attention but remains prescription-only; self-medicating without clinician assessment risks adverse effects and antiviral resistance. Antiviral use depends on illness severity, onset timing, and risk factors, not solely lab positivity. Eligible patients include those over 65, children under 5, pregnant or postpartum women, immunocompromised individuals, and people with heart, lung, diabetes, kidney, or liver disease. For eligible patients, antiviral treatment should be started early with correct dosing and duration. Otherwise, management is supportive: rest, fluids, fever control, and close monitoring. Seek care for persistent high fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, or dehydration.

triage.headline_ja: A型インフルエンザが増加、タミフルの自己判断服用に注意
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの通常範囲内の増加であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められず、公衆衛生上の重大な懸念も示されていない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザAの増加とタミフルの適正使用・自己判断服用への注意喚起が主旨であり、感染症危機管理上の異常事態を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Don't treat suspected cases at home, experts tell Nigerians
article.articleSummary: Public health physicians urge Nigerians not to treat suspected Ebola at home; seek prompt medical care to prevent complications and curb transmission. Nigeria has confirmed one imported Bundibugyo virus disease case in the Federal Capital Territory (Abuja), the fifth country to detect the outbreak since it began in the Democratic Republic of Congo on May 15, 2026. Laboratory confirmation was on October 20 for a woman with recent travel to Uganda; her symptoms began October 7, four days after arriving in Nigeria, and she sought treatment on October 11. She is in isolation; 44 contacts are being monitored; infection prevention and control measures have been strengthened at the facility she visited. The World Health Organization describes Bundibugyo virus disease as a severe and often fatal form of Ebola. Investigations aim to reconstruct the travel and exposure history to identify the source.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱:疑い例を自宅で治療しないようナイジェリア国民に専門家が呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生したブンディブギョウイルス病（エボラの一種）がウガンダ経由でナイジェリアに越境し、5カ国目の発生国となった国際的拡大事例であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアでの輸入症例だが、ナイジェリア（対象国リスト外）での確定例であり、発生源であるDRC（対象国リストに含まれる）のアウトブレイクに起因する越境事例。ウガンダ・ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : le Nigeria renforce les contrôles sanitaires à l'aéroport de Lagos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Nigeria strengthens health screening at Lagos airport
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola variant detected in Nigeria; Lagos airport screening strengthened after first Nigerian case confirmed on 20 October. A woman who arrived in Abuja from Uganda on 3 October developed symptoms four days later; lab confirmation led to isolation. Authorities identified 44 contacts and continue tracing; infection source undetermined. This follows the Bundibugyo outbreak declared in DRC in May 2026, with spread to multiple African countries; Kenya reported cases linked to an imported case. WHO Africa regional director Mohamed Janabi called the situation more complex. Nigeria previously contained Ebola in 2014 within 21 days, recording 19 cases and 7 deaths; authorities activated crisis management and boosted surveillance. WHO urges regional vigilance, stronger entry screening, and thorough follow-up of exposed individuals.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：ナイジェリアがラゴス空港での衛生検査を強化
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、エボラ（ブンディブギョ株）が複数国に拡大している国際的に重大な公衆衛生イベントであるため。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニアでの症例が報じられているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCは2026年5月に宣言されたブンディブギョ株エボラ流行の発生源として言及されているため含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Governo suíço nega viagem de paciente com ebola ao Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swiss government denies travel of a patient with Ebola to the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak extends to four African nations, with a Nigeria-diagnosed case—the first in more than a decade—and Africa CDC reporting thousands of deaths. The patient is a Uganda-born woman who is married to a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja and was diagnosed in Nigeria. Switzerland initially suggested she may have contracted Ebola during a trip through Uganda with her husband, but later stated the couple did not visit the Democratic Republic of Congo. Ugandan officials had previously suggested she could have traversed eastern Congo, yet WHO and Africa CDC say there is no official data confirming that travel route. Uganda had previously reported dozens of cases imported from the Congo border, though WHO had declared Uganda Ebola-free months before the Nigeria incident.

triage.headline_ja: スイス政府、エボラ患者のコンゴ渡航を否定
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ4カ国にまたがるエボラ流行拡大で、10年以上ぶりとなるナイジェリアでの症例確認やスイス人外交官家族の越境移動が絡み国際的注目度が高く、IHR基準も複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスにも関連するが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。DRC国境からの感染輸入歴が言及されており、同国での流行継続が示唆される。ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスは対象国外のためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Ilesanmi Says Nigeria Can Curb Outbreak As Akyala Faults Surveillance Gaps
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Nigeria: Nigeria can curb outbreak, says epidemiologist Olayinka Ilesanmi, citing trained personnel and prior outbreak experience; calls for centralized, verified information from Africa CDC and health authorities to avoid mixed messages and maintain public confidence; stresses cross-border collaboration with Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and airlines to map the index case's movements and identify contacts. Professor Adamu Akyala highlights surveillance gaps, pointing to the index case's travel from DRC to Uganda and then Abuja, where she encountered multiple healthcare facilities before diagnosis; surveillance not active; private hospitals underrepresented; need system expansion to private and public hospitals. Advocates vaccine research investment, presidential initiative to regain manufacturing capacity; warns against treating Ebola as solely an African issue; public gatherings not banned now; promote awareness. Symptoms: fever, severe headache, body weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea; urge medical care and hospital assessment; emphasize handwashing and hygiene.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：イレサンミ氏、ナイジェリアは流行を抑制可能と発言、一方アキャラ氏はサーベイランスの不備を指摘
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアでエボラ出血熱の症例が発生し、国境を越えた感染者の移動経路とサーベイランス体制の不備が指摘されており、IHR基準の複数項目（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア（アブジャ）でのエボラ症例であり、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRC・ウガンダは感染者の移動経路として言及されているのみで、発生国として確認できないため verified_locations には含めなかった。

article.articleHeadline: Cow suspected of rabies dies, nearly 500 in UP village get vaccines
article.articleSummary: Rabies scare in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, after a cow suspected of rabies died on Oct 20. Milk from the ill animal was used to prepare panchamrit for Navratri prayers and tea at a village fair, prompting vaccination of nearly 500 residents. About 70 villagers walked 11 km to CHC Gola for the first dose; the next day a village vaccination camp was set up, with over 450 more receiving their first dose. The second dose is due about a week later. The cow had been unwell for nearly a month; a government veterinary doctor suspected rabies on Oct 19. The stray dog likely involved remains untraceable, increasing anxiety. Rabies transmits mainly via saliva, not food, and pasteurisation/boiling kills the virus.

triage.headline_ja: 狂犬病感染が疑われる牛が死亡、ウッタル・プラデーシュ州の村で約500人がワクチン接種
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病感染が疑われる牛1頭による地域的な予防的ワクチン接種事例であり、人への確定感染例はなく、国際的拡大や渡航・貿易制限のリスクも認められない。
triage.notes: 牛の狂犬病は未確定（疑い段階）で、ヒト感染例は報告されていない。現地保健当局が既に予防接種対応を実施しており、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Africa at risk of continent-wide Ebola crisis, health chief warns
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, first detected in DR Congo in May, has become a continent-wide crisis with more than 4,600 deaths and cases spreading to central, eastern, and western Africa. Nigeria confirmed its first Bundibugyo case, despite not being on an initial risk list; Kenya has nine cases; Uganda reported 20 cases and was declared free of Ebola in August. Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya warns initial assessments underestimated the threat and cautions that every region of Africa could be affected. The response is being reorganized, with cross-border measures discussed and a plan to distribute responsibilities among regional bodies and partners ahead of a summit to secure funding commitments. There is no proven vaccine for Bundibugyo. Border closures are not recommended, as informal routes would persist.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ大陸全体でエボラ危機拡大の恐れ、保健当局トップが警告
triage.triage_reason: ブンディブギョ型エボラがDRCを起点に複数国へ拡大し死者4,600人超、IHR基準・WPRO基準とも複数該当かつ国際的関心が高いためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCで最初に検出されたブンディブギョ型エボラのアフリカ大陸規模への拡大を主題としているが、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: CDC Will Require All International Air Travelers to Fill Out Ebola Declaration, as Confirmed Deaths Top 4,690
article.articleSummary: All inbound international air travelers to the United States must attest they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the prior 21 days, effective November 3, 2026, 11:59 pm EST. Attestation may be digital or paper and must be completed before boarding; airlines will verify entries, and false statements may incur criminal penalties. The CDC previously invoked emergency powers to curb entry from the DRC; travelers from Uganda or South Sudan must enter only through designated airports (Dulles, JFK, Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta) with enhanced screening. A Nigerian case is believed linked to a passenger who transited through the DRC. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus drives what is described as the second-largest outbreak, spreading rapidly. As of Oct 21, there have been 9,735 cases and 4,690 confirmed deaths (actual toll may be higher); most cases in DRC, with clusters in Uganda and Kenya, plus confirmed cases in Nigeria and France.

triage.headline_ja: CDC、確定死者数が4,690人を超える中、すべての国際航空旅行者にエボラ申告書の記入を義務付けへ
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生中のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が急速拡大し症例9,735人・死亡4,690人に達し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスにも拡大、米国がCDC緊急措置として渡航制限を導入しておりIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス、米国、ジョージア州・バージニア州・ニューヨーク州等が含まれるが、これらは対象国リストに該当しないため除外。主要発生国はDRCであり、同国を唯一のverified_locationとした。

article.articleHeadline: US raises Kenya travel advisory over Ebola as Nairobi assures visitors
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease is active in Kenya, prompting a U.S. Kenya travel advisory raised to Level 3 (Reconsider travel) on Oct 19, 2026, based on a CDC Travel Health Notice. The notice warns of confirmed Kenyan cases, ongoing contact tracing, and recommends precautions, avoiding contact with symptomatic individuals, isolation if fever or other symptoms develop, and seeking guidance. Kenyan authorities report nine cases under quarantine; warnings emphasize border surveillance over full travel bans due to economic and social considerations. In Nigeria, the first Ebola case in 12 years involves a foreign national who travelled via Uganda; symptoms began Oct 7, care sought Oct 11 in Abuja, with infection confirmed as Bundibugyo. Nigeria has 44 people under active surveillance. Ghana issues enhanced surveillance; regional context includes ongoing DRC Ebola activity and new Kenya/Nigeria cases.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、ケニアでのエボラ出血熱を受け渡航勧告を引き上げ、ナイロビは訪問者に安全性を保証
triage.triage_reason: エボラ（ブンディブギョ型）がケニアで確認され米国が渡航レベル3に引き上げ、ナイジェリアでも12年ぶりの症例が発生するなど複数国に拡大しており、国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限が現実化しているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主たる発生国はケニアとナイジェリアだが、両国とも対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは『ongoing DRC Ebola activity』として進行中の発生が明記されているため含めた。ガーナは『enhanced surveillance』のみで確定症例の記載がないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Pacienta cu Ebola din Nigeria nu a călătorit în RD Congo, afirmă guvernul elvețian
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola patient from Nigeria did not travel to DR Congo, the Swiss government says.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola virus disease outbreak has seen Nigeria confirm its first case in over a decade, extending the outbreak to four African countries: DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. The Nigerian patient, wife of a Ugandan-origin Swiss diplomat, presented symptoms in Nigeria. Swiss authorities say she and her husband did not travel to DR Congo; Ugandan officials say she contracted Ebola in Uganda, where no active cases are reported. WHO and Africa CDC have not confirmed travel to DR Congo. Uganda had 20 cases in May–June, mostly linked to RDC; WHO declared Uganda Ebola-free in August. The Nigerian case involves the Bundibugyo strain, the same lineage circulating in DR Congo; 44 contacts have been identified. Africa CDC estimates about 4,700 deaths from the current outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリアのエボラ患者はコンゴ民主共和国に渡航していない、とスイス政府が発表
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC起源からウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリアへ拡大し、ナイジェリアでは10年以上ぶりの症例確認。国際的拡大・重大な公衆衛生リスクがあり、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスでの感染経路調査だが、これら3カ国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは流行の起源国・同一株（Bundibugyo株）の継続流行国として記事に明記されているため含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Schweizerin steckt sich mit Ebola an
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swiss woman contracts Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Swiss woman contracts Ebola in Nigeria, marking the country’s first Ebola case in more than a decade. The patient is Uganda-born wife of a Swiss diplomat stationed in Abuja and is being treated in Nigeria; nationality confirmed by the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs. Infection likely occurred during a joint trip with her husband in Uganda, but travel details are contested: Ugandan authorities say she was in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, while the EDA, WHO, and Africa CDC report no confirmed information of Congo travel. Uganda reports no current Ebola cases; earlier May–June Uganda had 20 cases, largely Congo-imported, and WHO declared Uganda Ebola-free in August. Nigeria’s case is part of an Africa-wide outbreak that Africa CDC says has affected four countries—DRC, Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria—with about 4,700 deaths confirmed to date.

triage.headline_ja: スイス人女性がエボラ出血熱に感染
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアで10年ぶりのエボラ症例が発生し、アフリカ複数国（DRC、ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア）にまたがる大規模アウトブレイク（死者約4700人）の一部であり、国際的な人の移動（スイス人外交官夫人）も絡むため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア（対象国リスト外）での症例だが、アフリカ全域のアウトブレイク（DRC含む4か国、死者約4700人）の一部として明示的に言及されているため、DRCを対象国として含めた。ウガンダ・ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。渡航歴についてウガンダ当局とWHO/Africa CDC/スイス外務省の間で情報が食い違っており、詳細不明。

article.articleHeadline: 나이지리아 첫 에볼라 감염 경로 두고 스위스·우간다 공방
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Switzerland and Uganda spar over the transmission route of Nigeria's first Ebola case
article.articleSummary: Two Ebola cases with cross-border links raise questions about transmission routes. Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola case is suspected to have contracted the virus during travel from Uganda; the patient, Ugandan-born and living in Abuja with a Swiss diplomat husband, vacationed in Uganda since mid-August and returned earlier this month. Nigeria is tracing 44 contacts; no secondary cases have been reported. Switzerland claims the infection occurred in Uganda, while Uganda says there are no active Ebola cases at home and that the patient may have visited the Democratic Republic of Congo’s outbreak area; WHO says it has no information of other countries visited. Separately, Kenya’s first Ebola case—the Kenyan who had lived in the DRC—died on Oct 5 after returning via Uganda; Kenya is tracing 135 contacts, with eight confirmed cases to date. The DRC outbreak totals exceed 9,500 cases and 4,600 deaths; Uganda’s May outbreak ended with WHO verification in August.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア初のエボラ感染経路を巡りスイス・ウガンダが対立
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の複数（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大）に該当し、DRCで9,500例超・4,600人超の死亡という大規模流行が継続中であるため、フルリスク評価に進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニアでの症例だが、これらは対象国リストに含まれない。DRCは進行中の大規模アウトブレイクの発生源として言及されているため対象国として記載。感染経路を巡りスイスとウガンダ政府間で見解の相違があり、外交的緊張も発生している。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Swiss government says Nigeria's patient likely contracted virus in Uganda
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease case in Nigeria's capital Abuja marks the first confirmed infection there in more than a decade. The patient is a Ugandan-born woman married to a Swiss diplomat, treated at a private clinic in Abuja. She reportedly visited Uganda about two weeks before diagnosis and returned to Abuja around October 3. Investigators, with Nigeria and Uganda, WHO, and Africa CDC, are reconstructing travel history to identify the infection source; no confirmed evidence yet that she travelled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the origin of the current outbreak. The woman’s husband is in isolation but asymptomatic. Uganda reports no active cases; in May–June, 20 Ebola cases linked to infections imported from DRC, with Uganda’s outbreak declared over in August. Health authorities continue contact tracing and facility exposure assessments in Abuja.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：スイス政府、ナイジェリアの患者はウガンダでウイルスに感染した可能性が高いと発表
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアの首都で10年以上ぶりとなるエボラ確定例が発生し、WHO・アフリカCDC・複数国が関与する国際調査が進行中であり、重篤な公衆衛生リスクと国際的拡大の懸念がある。
triage.notes: 本事例の主題はナイジェリア（首都アブジャ）での感染例であり、感染源とされるウガンダ、および背景として言及されたコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）の進行中アウトブレイクは本記事の直接の発生地ではないため、対象国リスト上のverified_locationsには該当国なし。ナイジェリア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: Lapas Salemba periksa 900 warga binaan untuk deteksi dini TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Salemba Prison screens 900 inmates for early detection of tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: Salemba Correctional Facility (Class IIA), Central Jakarta, in collaboration with Puskesmas Cempaka Putih, screened 900 inmates and all staff for early detection of tuberculosis (TB). The program aims to safeguard inmate and staff health and prevent transmission. Screenings run in stages from October 13 to October 23, 2026, with a daily quota of 100 persons. Each participant underwent diabetes glucose testing and chest X-ray as part of a general health screening to identify TB indicators. If any results warranted further attention, health professionals would follow established medical procedures. The effort underscores strengthened prevention and healthcare services for the Salemba inmate population and employees, reflecting a professional and humane approach to fulfilling inmates' health rights. The partnership highlights ongoing TB surveillance in Jakarta.

triage.headline_ja: サレンバ刑務所、結核早期発見のため収容者900人を検査
triage.triage_reason: 通常の結核スクリーニング活動の報告であり、異常事態や重症例の急増、国際的拡大のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 刑務所内での定期的なTBスクリーニングプログラムの報告であり、アウトブレイクや異常な感染拡大を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Liberia: 'We Are Closely Monitoring the Regional Situation' - NPHIL Boss Says As They Urge Vigilance Amid Ebola Scare in West Africa
article.articleSummary: Liberia reports no confirmed Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) case as of 23 October 2026, but the government through NPHIL and the Ministry of Health is closely monitoring the regional Ebola situation centered in West Africa, including Nigeria. A new travel advisory requires health-surveillance forms and accurate health/travel history. Travelers arriving from or transiting via the DRC will undergo 21 days of self-isolation with daily monitoring; those from Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria face the same 21-day monitoring. All entrants will undergo health screening, including temperature checks. Ebola symptoms include fever, severe headache, weakness, fatigue, muscle and body pains, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach pain, skin rash; bleeding may occur. NPHIL is strengthening surveillance at Roberts International Airport and border points, procuring lab reagents, expanding testing capacity, and coordinating with agencies. The National Reference Laboratory was connected to the national grid on 19 October 2026, improving operations; report suspicious cases to 4455 or call ambulance 5888.

triage.headline_ja: リベリア:「地域情勢を注視している」- NPHIL責任者、西アフリカでのエボラ警戒の中で警戒を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: リベリア国内に確定症例はないものの、西アフリカ地域（ナイジェリア含む）でのエボラ出血熱の流行懸念を受け、DRC・ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアからの入国者に対し21日間の自己隔離を義務付ける渡航制限措置が既に実施されており、IHR基準の複数項目（深刻性・異常性・国際拡散リスク・渡航制限）に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はリベリアによる地域監視体制の強化であり、リベリア国内での確定症例はない。『西アフリカで中心となっている地域のエボラ情勢』はナイジェリア（対象国リスト外）が主に言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれるDRCも渡航制限対象国として明記されているため検証対象地域に含めた。ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: AMA and EMA issue joint guidance on Ebola vaccine development | European Medicines Agency (EMA)
article.articleSummary: EMA's Emergency Task Force (ETF) and the African Medicines Agency (AMA) published a joint position paper to accelerate clinical trials for vaccines against Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Triggered by the public health emergency in the DRC with cases detected in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria, the paper sets minimum requirements to start trials and guides design, with emphasis on rigorous safeguards and timely regulatory approvals by African NRAs. It notes that for well-characterised platforms (e.g., mRNA, viral-vector), some animal toxicity studies may be postponed or waived if prior safety data exist. Early trials should occur in Africa to streamline transition to Phase II/III, including non-human challenge studies to pre-screen efficacy. A single-dose vaccine is preferred for rapid deployment. The Phase III pivotal study envisions ring vaccination of contacts, evaluating multiple candidates, with safety data from adults informing studies in children and pregnant women. Regulators should engage early.

triage.headline_ja: AMA(アフリカ医薬品庁)とEMA(欧州医薬品庁)がエボラワクチン開発に関する共同ガイダンスを発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生したブンディブギョウイルスによるエボラ出血熱の公衆衛生緊急事態がウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアにも拡大しており、国際的な規制当局が共同でワクチン開発を加速する事態となっている。
triage.notes: 本記事はEMA/AMAによるワクチン開発ガイダンスが主題だが、背景にDRCで発生しウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへ拡大したエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョウイルス）の公衆衛生緊急事態が存在する。対象国リストにはDRCのみ含まれるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。実際のアウトブレイクの詳細（症例数・死亡者数等）については本サマリーに記載がなく、フルRRAでの確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria Confirms 1st Ebola Case in 12 Years
article.articleSummary: 1 Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) case confirmed in Abuja, Nigeria, the first in 12 years. On Oct 20, 2026, lab confirmed in a woman who arrived from Uganda; symptoms began Oct 7; admitted Oct 11; she has been isolated and is receiving care. Public health authorities identified 44 contacts—including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers, and travel contacts—for monitoring. Response coordinated by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and the Federal Ministry of Health, with hospital support to strengthen infection prevention and control. Nationwide high alert issued; facilities urged to promptly identify, isolate, and report suspected cases; emphasis on hand hygiene and avoiding contact with blood and bodily fluids. Transmission is via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids of symptomatic individuals or contaminated objects; incubation 2–21 days. Context: ongoing Central Africa Ebola outbreaks, Kenya reported an imported Bundibugyo virus case linked to the DRC outbreak; Nigeria's 2014 Lagos outbreak is recalled.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア、12年ぶりにエボラ出血熱の症例を確認
triage.triage_reason: 12年ぶりのナイジェリアでのエボラ確認例であり、ウガンダからの輸入例・接触者44名の存在など国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生上の深刻性が認められるため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア（非対象国）での症例であり、ウガンダからの輸入例、ケニアでの別症例、DRCでの進行中流行は文脈情報として言及されているのみで、各国が記事の主要発生地とは言えないため、対象国リストに該当する verified_locations はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola risk: All air passengers to US should certify they haven't been to DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola risk prompts tightened travel controls as of 2026-10-23. The Bundibugyo strain has spread beyond the Democratic Republic of Congo to four other countries, with Nigeria the latest affected and France reporting a non-African case. In the United States, from November 4 all air passengers must certify they have not visited DR Congo in the prior 21 days. Non-US citizens who have been to Uganda or South Sudan within 21 days will be denied entry; US citizens who have been to those countries but not in DR Congo within 21 days will be routed through designated airports (e.g., Washington Dulles) for health screening. Other countries have monitoring: India requires health monitoring and isolation if symptomatic for travellers from Ebola-affected areas (call 1075). Thailand, Mexico, United Kingdom, Nigeria, Kenya and Uganda implement airport screening, thermal scans and health declarations. A flyer returning to Abuja from Uganda tested positive, illustrating ongoing transmission.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱のリスク:米国行きの全航空便乗客はコンゴ民主共和国に渡航していないことを証明する必要がある
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）がDRCから複数国に拡大し、米国等が渡航制限措置を導入するなど、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する重大な国際的懸念事案。
triage.notes: Thailand、Indiaは空港スクリーニング等の対応措置の対象国として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではないため除外。ナイジェリア・フランス・ウガンダ・南スーダン等は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の輸入症例であり、ウガンダからナイジェリアへの国際的な感染拡大の可能性を示す異常事例でIHR基準を複数満たすため。
triage.notes: 発生国はナイジェリア、感染経路はウガンダ渡航歴によるものだが、両国とも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空。DRCは渡航していないと明記されているため除外。

article.articleHeadline: حمى الكسلان.. فيروس استوائي تثيره حشرات "الهاموش" في أمريكا اللاتينية - اليوم السابع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sloth fever... a tropical virus transmitted by 'hamoosh' insects in Latin America - Youm7
article.articleSummary: Oropouche fever, a tropical virus in Latin America and the Caribbean, is spreading again, transmitted mainly by tiny biting insects called hamoosh. Brazil's Amazon basin remains heavily affected, with transmission also reported in Panama, Peru, Colombia, and Cuba, among others. As of August 2025, PAHO reported 12,786 confirmed cases across 11 countries from the start of the year to July 27; 2024 saw over 16,000 confirmed cases in the region. Symptoms usually begin abruptly with high fever, severe headache, chills, myalgia, and joint pains, sometimes with nausea, vomiting, and rash. Clinical pictures resemble dengue and chikungunya, complicating differentiation without laboratory tests. Most recover, but rare neurological complications such as meningitis or encephalitis occur; potential pregnancy risks and fetal outcomes require further study. There is no licensed vaccine or antiviral; management is supportive, focusing on symptom relief and vector control. Deforestation and changes in land use may increase human–vector contact and regional spread.

triage.headline_ja: 怠け病熱…ラテンアメリカで『ハムーシュ』昆虫が媒介する熱帯ウイルス
triage.triage_reason: オロプーシュ熱がブラジルを含む中南米複数国で拡大中だが、重症度は低く社会的関心の高まりも明記されておらず、フルRRAに進めるには情報が不足している。
triage.notes: 発生地域にキューバ、パナマ、ペルー、コロンビアが含まれるが、いずれも対象国リストに該当しないため除外。ブラジル（アマゾン流域）が主要な発生地として記載されている。
